chapter: Memphis boyhood and the Ohio territory years
title: Jimmy Lunceford, the athletic instructor who formed the band
summary: Crawford describes Lunceford's Fisk and Columbia background, his return to Memphis, and the band's summers at Lakeside and move north to Cleveland.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Now, I started out, as I forestated, with an orchestra leader (inaudible). He was an athletic instructor there, Jimmy Lunsford. He finished Fisk University, and then he came to New York. Pardon me. He took up postgraduate work at Columbia University, and also he tried to join Fletcher Henderson's band, but he didn't make it.

So he came back to Memphis. Now, he finished Fisk University, which was in Nashville, but he came back to Memphis to accept a job there as athletic instructor. The man was a natural athlete, a good musician, and above all he was one of the greatest gentlemen that I ever met in my life. I loved the man. He's dead now, of course, and we started out from scratch.

And all of a sudden -- we used to go to Lakeside, Ohio. That's right off Lake Erie, right on Lake Erie -- for about three or four summer seasons, and finally round about 1929, Stanley, we decided to go North, you know, go further north. So we went to Cleveland, Ohio. We had a job there to go on, Willie's Lakeshore Garden. That was the most popular place in Cleveland.
